question.problem: Given that $u=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]$ is a non-zero  vector that is orthogonal to the set $W=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ -10\end{aligned}]\},$ find the value of $\frac{a+c}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $u$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $u\cdot {w}_{1}=0$ and $u\cdot {w}_{2}=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}u\cdot {w}_{1}=0 \\ u\cdot {w}_{2}=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-10{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$

with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & -2 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & -1 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -10 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-6){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{1}{2} & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd), so ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{4}{3}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=\frac{5}{3}{x}_{3}.$ So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{3}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{4}{3}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Setting ${x}_{3}=3,$ we get the vector 
$[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

Therefore, we obtain $a=5,$ $b=4,$ and $c=3.$

Finally, $\frac{a+c}{b}=\frac{5+3}{4}=2.$
